summary: The classic encoder-decoder diagram names the main parts of the 2017 transformer correctly. The words and attention arcs are prepared examples; no attention matrix, translation, or next-word inference is calculated.

claims.claim: The classic diagram follows the 2017 encoder-decoder architecture.
claims.how: The box labels include embedding, position, masked self-attention, encoder attention, add and norm, feed-forward, linear, and softmax.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.says: The encoder-decoder architecture combines embeddings, positions, attention, feed-forward layers, residual normalization, and output probabilities. Decoder self-attention masks later tokens.

claims.claim: The toy presents prepared next-word and translation examples.
claims.how: MAT and the MUNDO tile label are literal outputs, and arc strengths are stored. The How-to and About now say that these are prepared examples.

claims.claim: The first attention picture is schematic rather than a causal decoder calculation.
claims.how: Some arcs lead to later token positions; there is no QK product, mask, normalization, or learned attention value.

claims.note: For a numerical next-token view, add masked softmax attention and label the probabilities.

simplified: MAT and MUNDO are stored outputs. Arc strengths are fixed, not attention probabilities. The first picture permits links to later tokens, so it should not be read as causal decoder attention.

fixes.what: Replace the prediction labels with prepared-example labels and state that words and attention strengths are stored.
Make the diagram key describe MUNDO as the end of a prepared example, consistent with the help text.
A numerical decoder view could calculate masked attention and probabilities, with its learned or chosen weights identified.
